cases.input: A chain protects only /api/**; a newly exposed export controller lives at /exports.
expected: Identify unmatched-chain exposure, inspect its actual mapping and introduce the intended catch-all policy with positive and negative tests. A rule inside the /api chain cannot protect /exports.

cases.input: A security test passes because /api/private does not exist and returns 404.
expected: Reject this as authorization evidence. Test a known protected operation or explicit probe under the real chain, including a working positive control.

cases.input: The mapper copies every realm/client role to an admin authority for the app.
expected: Require mapping from trusted intended issuer/client authorities only, test absent/wrong roles, and do not infer resource ownership from authentication.

cases.input: A session-based BFF performs only local database CRUD; request Spring Security best practices.
expected: Preserve the session model. Do not add a browser JWT, extra bearer filter or refresh scheduler without a token-using requirement.

cases.input: An implementation proposes disabling CSRF because all requests use JSON REST.
expected: Reject the credential-blind justification. Retain protection for session-authenticated unsafe operations and local logout, with real token lifecycle tests.

cases.input: A new supported Spring version offers SPA integration, but a legacy custom handler is copied unchanged.
expected: Verify selected APIs and prefer their supported integration, or justify the custom handler. Test raw/masked token compatibility and renewal after login/logout.

cases.input: Only MockMvc csrf() tests pass; frontend never obtains a token.
expected: Do not report browser CSRF as verified. Require real acquisition/transport and subsequent mutation tests; mark unavailable runtime NOT_RUN.

cases.input: An intentionally public non-credentialed endpoint returns identical public data with wildcard CORS.
expected: Do not assign automatic HIGH severity to the wildcard. Verify the exposure and credential model; distinguish it from credentialed private-data access.

cases.input: Private session API reflects arbitrary Origin and allows credentials.
expected: Trace browser-readable sensitive data and the actual CORS policy; require a constrained origin policy with a negative cross-origin test and evidence-based severity.

cases.input: A confidential OIDC client has a secret; implementation assumes PKCE is therefore already active.
expected: Verify real transaction-specific PKCE S256 and supported client settings. A secret is not evidence of a PKCE exchange.

cases.input: oauth2Login is configured and a downstream API uses an expired access token.
expected: Trace the authorized-client manager/provider, caller and renewed credential storage. Require expiry/refresh/failure evidence, not a claim that login config proves refresh.

cases.input: An IdP timeout triggers deleting every session and retrying the same downstream payment.
expected: Distinguish transient failure from invalid_grant. Apply bounded policy and do not replay uncertain non-idempotent work without deduplication.

cases.input: Keycloak disables an account; an already-authenticated BFF session still works.
expected: Do not assume automatic immediate synchronization. Establish and test the chosen disable/role-change propagation mechanism and latency.

cases.input: Back-channel logout is enabled while cookie names, registry and multi-node session storage differ from defaults.
expected: Check the selected version and actual cookie/registry/session-store integration; test the relevant session and replicas. No assumption that local registry invalidates every node.

cases.input: The local session cookie is removed and report says logged out everywhere.
expected: Require supported server context/session/credential cleanup and distinguish local from IdP/global logout. Test old-session reuse and IdP failure behavior.

cases.input: Supported RP logout sends an id_token_hint only to the configured provider.
expected: Do not confuse this explicit protocol exception with exposing access/refresh tokens to the SPA. Review destination, URL redaction and selected logout requirements; never use ID token as an API credential.

cases.input: A valid user can supply another userId to create or update a payment.
expected: Derive/validate authorization server-side, protect mapped owner fields and test actual cross-user records with valid session and valid CSRF.

cases.input: A cross-user write test returns 403 only because CSRF is absent; repository update is unscoped.
expected: Reject false ownership assurance. Repeat with valid attacker-session CSRF and assert denial without DB or outbound side effects.

cases.input: Detail lookup is owner-scoped but counts, exports, cache keys and job output are global.
expected: Trace all relevant secondary paths and deny cross-user disclosure; no generic full audit of unrelated modules.

cases.input: Only BFF callback errors are counted as failed passwords, with no Keycloak brute-force policy.
expected: Identify the wrong enforcement layer. Require actual IdP failure threshold/reset/wait/recovery plus separate session/rate policies, tested with synthetic users.

cases.input: X-Forwarded-For controls throttling and backend is directly reachable from the internet.
expected: Verify trusted ingress and direct-port reachability; reject client-chosen source identity. Require boundary tests and distinguish rate limiting from DDoS protection.

cases.input: A JWT decoder validates signature and issuer but not the intended API audience; tests use jwt() mocks.
expected: Require audience and token-profile validation with a real decoder test; distinguish mock authorities from cryptographic validation. Do not migrate the browser BFF.

cases.input: A STATELESS chain accepts an auth token from an automatically sent cookie; CSRF is disabled.
expected: Identify ambient credentials despite statelessness. Require appropriate anti-forgery protection or a genuinely separate non-ambient bearer model.

cases.input: Only a static frontend spacing change is requested; no browser identity/data/rendering boundary changes.
expected: Do not load every Spring security reference, create new agents or run a full security audit. Preserve relevant normal checks and existing decisions.
